tool_input.command:
S="<workspace>/sparq-legacy-modernization/skills/modernization-assessment/scripts"; O=modernization-assessment
python3 "$S/extract.py" . --out $O && for p in "inventory 01-inventory.md" "edges 02a-edge-tables.md" "deadcode 05a-dead-code-candidates.md" "waveseed 03a-wave-seed.md" "wavedraft 03a-waves-draft.json"; do set -- $p; python3 "$S/render.py" $1 $O/graph.json --out $O/$2; done; find app -type f | head -50; wc -c $O/*

P="<workspace>/sparq-legacy-modernization/skills/modernization-assessment/scripts/render.py"; G=modernization-assessment/graph.json
python3 "$P" inventory $G --out modernization-assessment/01-inventory.md
python3 "$P" edges $G --out modernization-assessment/02a-edge-tables.md
python3 "$P" deadcode $G --out modernization-assessment/05a-dead-code-candidates.md
python3 "$P" waveseed $G --out modernization-assessment/03a-wave-seed.md
python3 "$P" wavedraft $G --out modernization-assessment/03a-waves-draft.json
cat -n app/cbl/PROGA.cbl app/cbl/PROGB.cbl; cat $G; cat modernization-assessment/03a-wave-seed.md modernization-assessment/03a-waves-draft.json modernization-assessment/05a-dead-code-candidates.md

result:
The scan produced no waves, because the tree has nothing to sequence. It holds two COBOL programs, `PROGA` (7 lines) and `PROGB` (4 lines), and no JCL, scheduler, CICS definitions, copybooks or datasets. `PROGA` calls `PROGB` statically at `app/cbl/PROGA.cbl:6`. That is the only edge. The artifacts are in `./modernization-assessment/`. The JSON files validate, the citation check is clean, and the run marker is set to done.

**Largest risk:** "the nightly batch cycle" maps to nothing in the tree. There is no job, scheduler or dataset, so the scan can't say what the cycle runs, in what order, or on what data. Both programs are marked low port difficulty. `PROGA`'s blast radius is medium because it may be the cycle's driver. Nothing is unreachable or dormant, so both programs are dead-code "unknown" and every dead-code claim is provisional. The tree has no git history, so dormancy was never measured.

**Top open questions for the client's engineers:**
1. Which JCL job or scheduler entry runs the nightly cycle? Is `PROGA` its driver, or a test fixture? `PROGA` prints `CALL FAILED IF WE GET HERE` before it calls `PROGB` (`app/cbl/PROGA.cbl:5`), and `PROGB` only does `GOBACK`.
2. Was other source left out, such as JCL, procs, copybooks, a CICS definition or a Control-M export? The extractor saw none of them. Nothing was listed as not parsed.
3. Do archived outputs exist to serve as the oracle, such as GDG generations, SYSOUT, partner extracts or report archives?

You gave all three scoping flags, so no defaults were applied. No `--delivery` was given, so the estimate shows both the conventional and AI-assisted cases.

The estimate is roughly 3.5 to 14 days conventional and 3.25 to 12.5 days AI-assisted. It is wide because the real cost is the nightly cycle, which isn't in the tree. It assumes the cycle is only these two programs.

I also wrote `06-test-strategy.md`, which ranks the oracle options and lists what to ask the client for. It proposes one open deviation row (D-1) for the misleading `CALL FAILED` message, unapproved.
